profile.reading:
DataBank IAD2 sits at 1764A Old Meadow Lane, McLean, Virginia, DataBank's only Northern Virginia facility outside the Ashburn campus. DataBank's own IAD2 page states 40,690 square feet of IT space and 3 megawatts of critical IT load, with 8 onsite network carriers, an N+1 power and N+1 cooling design, and a 100 percent renewable energy sourcing claim, alongside FISMA, SOC 1/2, HIPAA, PCI-DSS, and ISO 27001 compliance certifications. DataBank markets IAD2 explicitly as a disaster-recovery and business-continuity site for its Ashburn customers, describing McLean as "perfectly situated between Washington, D.C. and Ashburn" and less than 30 minutes from IAD3, positioning it as a geographically diverse backup location for Ashburn-based tenants rather than a primary hyperscale campus in its own right. DataBank does not publish a year-opened date, a formal Uptime Institute Tier certification, or a named power utility for IAD2; Dominion Energy serves Fairfax County as a matter of public record but is not named on DataBank's own page. Fairfax County adopted a countywide Data Centers Zoning Ordinance Amendment effective September 11, 2024, following a Board of Supervisors-directed study process that began in 2023, reflecting the county's broader effort to manage data center growth and its environmental and infrastructure impacts as facilities like IAD2 sit within McLean's mixed office and light-industrial corridors near Tysons.

McLean sits within Fairfax County's Tysons-area commercial corridor, a mixed office and light-industrial submarket distinct from Loudoun County's much larger Ashburn data center concentration a short drive away. Fairfax County's 2024 zoning ordinance amendment for data centers reflects growing county-level attention to balancing continued commercial investment against community concerns over land use, traffic, and utility infrastructure as facilities like IAD2 operate within established suburban office parks rather than the purpose-built industrial campuses more common in Ashburn.

sources.title: Fairfax County, Virginia, Data Centers Zoning Ordinance

[process narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] This facility is attributed in the registry to DataBank. DataBank Ltd. was established in 2005 in a historic former Federal Reserve Bank building in downtown Dallas, Texas, that had been converted to a data center in 1999, per DataBank own corporate history page fetched this session. DataBank was acquired in July 2016 by a group of investors led by DigitalBridge, per that same page. DataBank own history page also lists a series of acquisitions expanding its footprint, three Salt Lake City area data centers from C7 Data Centers plus facilities in Cleveland and Pittsburgh from 365 Data Centers in January 2017, Lightbound, an Indianapolis based provider, in December 2018, United States and United Kingdom data center assets from zColo in December 2020, and four Houston area data centers from CyrusOne for 670 million dollars in January 2022. A trade press article fetched this session, from pe-insights.com, reports that DigitalBridge agreed to sell a 27 percent fully diluted equity stake in DataBank to Swiss Life Asset Management and EDF Invest for about 1.2 billion dollars, expected to close in the fourth quarter of 2022, reducing DigitalBridge own stake to about 15.5 percent and yielding DigitalBridge about 230 million dollars in cash proceeds. DataBank own history page states the company now operates more than 65 data centers across more than 27 markets. The operator own dedicated page for this facility, McLean, designated IAD2, fetched this session, gives its address as 1764A Old Meadow Lane, McLean, VA 22102, with 3 MW of critical IT load and 40,690 IT square feet, a figure independently repeated identically on the operator own Northern Virginia market overview page also fetched this session, a second internal confirmation of the same number.

reading.body:
DataBank's McLean IAD2 facility publishes 3 MW of IT capacity, placing it at the bottom of Virginia's published-capacity cohort and outside the scale where large AI training clusters are typically housed.

The facility spans 40,690 square feet of technical space, yielding roughly 74 watts per square foot. This density suggests mixed enterprise and colocation use rather than hyperscale infrastructure. At common AI training densities, 3 MW would support approximately 75 racks at 40 kW per rack, or roughly 300 racks at typical colocation power levels of 10 kW per rack. Neither figure reflects the operator's claim; both are derived from the single published capacity number. For perspective, a single large AI training cluster can consume this entire allocation on its own.

Virginia holds the largest installed data center capacity globally. This site has mapped 326 facilities in the state, but only 19 publish a megawatt figure. IAD2 ranks last among those 19, with the full published-MW cohort totaling 1,326 MW. That ranking reflects disclosed capacity only and omits facilities that have not published specifications. The McLean location adjacent to the Loudoun County corridor may carry network or compliance value not captured in published power figures.
